selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main warning in this passage?
questions.answer: A person should not make this short worldly life his biggest goal.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to someone who makes this temporary life his main purpose?
questions.answer: He is really in a state like Hell, even if his life looks pleasant on the outside.

questions.question: What kind of person receives happiness in both this life and the next?
questions.answer: A person who sincerely turns toward the eternal life.

questions.question: How does such a person look at this world?
questions.answer: He sees it as a place of waiting before Paradise.

questions.question: When life feels hard and painful, what does that person do?
questions.answer: He stays patient and thanks Allah.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage make between appearance and reality?
questions.answer: Something may look like Paradise on the outside, but a person can still be miserable inside.

questions.question: What does the word “fleeting” tell us about worldly life?
questions.answer: It does not last long.

questions.question: Why can a believer endure worldly troubles better, based on this passage?
questions.answer: Because he knows this world is temporary and looks ahead to Paradise.

questions.question: What two good actions are named for dealing with difficulty?
questions.answer: Patience and thankfulness.

questions.question: What is one lesson a Muslim student can learn from this passage?
questions.answer: We should live for the Hereafter and trust Allah during hard times.

questions.question: Which life does the passage teach us to take most seriously: this world or the eternal life?
questions.answer: The eternal life.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage describe about worldly life?
questions.answer: Treating it as the final goal.

questions.question: If a person’s life seems beautiful and comfortable, does that always mean he is truly happy?
questions.answer: No. He may still be in a very bad spiritual condition.

questions.question: What reward is mentioned for the one who truly aims for the next life?
questions.answer: Happiness in both worlds.

questions.question: How does thinking about Paradise help a person in hard times?
questions.answer: It helps him bear the hardship with patience.

questions.question: What does the passage show about sincere intention?
questions.answer: A right intention changes how a person lives and responds to suffering.

questions.question: What feeling should come with patience in this passage?
questions.answer: Thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: Why is this world compared to a waiting-room?
questions.answer: Because it is not the final home; it is only a temporary place before what comes next.

questions.question: What does “in all seriousness” tell us about turning toward eternal life?
questions.answer: A person must be sincere and truly committed.

questions.question: Write the big idea of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: If you live only for this world, you lose, but if you live for the Hereafter, you gain peace and happiness.

questions.question: What two ways of living are being compared in this passage?
questions.answer: Living for this world and living for the Hereafter.

questions.question: Which person is described as being like someone in Hell?
questions.answer: The one who makes temporary life his main aim.

questions.question: Does the passage say that an easy-looking life always brings real peace?
questions.answer: No. Outward comfort does not guarantee inner peace.

questions.question: Who gains joy in both places, not just one?
questions.answer: The person who seriously seeks eternal life.
